newsitem.title: USA: Eight bikers charged with murders, violence.
newsitem.headline: Eight bikers charged with murders, violence.

text.p: Eight members of the Outlaws motorcycle gang were arrested on Wednesday and charged with murder, bomb attacks and drug peddling as part of a criminal enterprise that operated throughout Florida, prosecutors said.
The men were arrested after a federal grand jury returned an indictment accusing the biker gang's chapters of criminal activities in Fort Lauderdale, Tampa, St. Petersburg, Orlando and Daytona Beach.
The U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration, FBI, Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco and Firearms and several state and local law enforcement agencies had been investigating the Outlaws for the past four years.
Officials said 18 other gang members have been convicted of drug, racketeering and firearm offences since 1994.

Among the eight men arrested were Clarence "Smitty" Smith, 52, and Wayne Hicks, 42, both former regional bosses of the Outlaws. Also arrested was Houston Murphy, 36, the current regional leader of the biker group.
Two other members of the Outlaws remained fugitives, prosecutors said.

The men are accused of executing a federal witness in a drug case in New Orleans in 1981, murdering four people in the Fort Lauderdale area in 1983, murdering the president of the rival Warlocks Motorcycle Club in Edgewater, Florida, in 1991 and bombing the clubhouse of a rival gang in Orlando in 1994.

"Violent gang behaviour poses a substantial threat to the citizens of our community," U.S. Attorney Charles Wilson said in a statement. "The Outlaws Motorcycle Club operated through acts of violence that involved repeated murders, attempted murders, arsons, robberies, extortions and other acts to intimidate citizens and to control the state of Florida."
If convicted of all the murder, drug and racketeering charges, each man could face up to life in prison.
The men will be tried by U.S. Judge Susan Bucklew in Tampa.
